answer: Each identity polishes one crystal lens to a mirror finish and locks an 80-credit bond. Each comet passage brings one blank per key, blocking stockpiles. An auditor measures the lens against the mirror standard within half a wavelength and verifies its serial. A reused serial or a mismatch burns the bond. The first lens costs 33 credits and the kth costs 33+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6027 and 1000 fakes cost 3,030,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-lens ring fails because a rented lens bears another key's serial. An honest agent pays 33 once and recovers the bond on audit.
